main_issue: Whether and when Agent D may cook strong-smelling fish curry in the shared kitchen; resolved as Saturdays only.

A-B.evidence: A asks for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B says the smell gets into clothes (T2) and later agrees Saturday works (T8). They never address each other directly, but both back the same arrangement.

A-C.evidence: C complains about the smell in the laundry (T3) and says 'Saturday works for me' (T9, repeated), matching A's Saturday proposal (T5).

A-D.evidence: A asks D to cook it on Saturdays (T5); D agrees 'I can cook it on Saturdays' (T6); A thanks D (T7). D moved from defending the food (T4) to accepting A's request.

B-C.evidence: Both complain about the smell (T2, T3) and both accept Saturday (T8, T9).

B-D.evidence: B complains (T2); D agrees to Saturdays (T6); B replies 'that works for me too' (T8).

C-D.evidence: C complains about the smell (T3); D has agreed to Saturdays (T6); C repeatedly says 'Saturday works for me' (T9, T25 and later).
